text:
IncidentBot: PAGER: p99 latency SLO breach on /v1/generate (prod-us-east-1). p99 observed 2.8s (SLO=1.0s). Alert fired 2026-03-14T18:08:08Z
Alice Chen: got the pager, moving this into incident thread. I'll start digging.
David Ortiz: I'm primary on-call, taking lead. Is this one model or wider?
Priya Nair: initial slices show the spike aligns with a quant profile rollout: `fp8-aggressive` applied to redwood-small-* canary at ~18:05 UTC. Canary checks passed but rollout continued.
Emma Li: CS: multiple customers reporting streaming stalls and partial responses. ACME Corp opened a Sev ticket (#2374) — they report chat delays.
Samir Patel: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panel=latency&env=prod-us-east-1&route=/v1/generate — see p95/p99 jump.
David Ortiz: Priya, pull the deployment audit and any runtime warnings.
Priya Nair: deployment audit: 2026-03-14T18:05:12Z deploy-bot applied quant_profile=fp8-aggressive to redwood-small-v3 canary, then gradual.
Priya Nair: runtime logs show a kernel path flip around 18:07:40 and a lot of memcopy/lock waits:
```
[18:07:40] runtime INFO: kernel_select -> prefer_fp8_kernels=true
[18:07:41] runtime WARN: kv_cache: shard memcpy latency increased
[18:07:42] runtime WARN: dequantize_shard waiting on kv_lock
```
Alice Chen: correlating traces — streaming requests that hit dequantize while kv-maintenance runs end up stalled for 200-800ms each chunk; some accumulate and cross the p99 threshold.
David Ortiz: mitigation options: 1) pause/rollback the fp8 rollout, 2) isolate canary and throttle it, 3) apply a runtime patch to avoid dequantize happening under kv_lock. Which is fastest?
Priya Nair: fastest is rollback to `fp16-conservative` for prod-us-east-1; we should pause any further rollouts. I'll prepare the rollback now.
Priya Nair: executing rollback (control plane API):
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/models/redwood-small-v3/reconfigure \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"quant_profile":"fp16-conservative","mode":"force"}'
```
DeployBot: Job job-9017 accepted, targeting 8 hosts in prod-us-east-1.
Priya Nair: job logs:
```
[18:12:05] host-07: stopping fp8 workers
[18:12:10] host-07: reloaded runtime (fp16 path)
[18:13:25] host-07: success
```
Priya Nair: rollback finished at 18:16:05 UTC across targeted hosts.
David Ortiz: I'm enabling an early-fail for streaming and capping canary traffic while we watch; this should reduce tail impact during healing.
David Ortiz: route change: set streaming.early_fail_threshold=2.5s for /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1.
Alice Chen: realtime metrics: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.05s within 3 minutes of rollback + early-fail. p95 back within SLO. Error rates for streaming dropped to baseline.
Emma Li: CS update sent — ACME notified of rollback and mitigation; they're seeing improved behavior. They've asked for a postmortem.
Samir Patel: root cause hypothesis? Need details for postmortem and action items.
Alice Chen: hypothesis: `fp8-aggressive` changed kernel/runtime behavior so dequantization runs on threads that also perform KV cache shard operations; dequantization attempted in-place while holding kv_lock causing serialization. Under streaming workload (lots of small chunked emits) this produced amplified tail latency. Also, missing fast-path for partial_flush meant retries/extra work.
Priya Nair: supporting log snippets:
```
[18:06:58] runtime WARN: dequantize_shard(): attempted in-place dequant while kv_lock held
[18:06:58] runtime DEBUG: kv_lock wait 256ms
[18:07:10] stream WARN: chunk_emit delayed 512ms
```
David Ortiz: actions: (A) immediate: rollback done — monitor; (B) short-term: add rollout guard in control plane to block `aggressive` quant profiles for models with streaming=true or routes marked realtime; (C) medium-term: code fix to decouple dequantize from kv_lock (hotfix/PR), add unit/integration tests simulating KV contention + dequant; (D) update canary policy to cap traffic and require streaming smoke tests.
Alice Chen: I'll author the postmortem and assign owners. Priya, please add the unit test and the rollout guard change to the control plane. Samir, add release checklist item for streaming stress tests.
Priya Nair: will add a nightly stress test that simulates interleaved KV maintenance and dequant flows; will also add the control plane guard and a config flag to opt-in explicitly to aggressive profiles.
IncidentBot: Incident RESOLVED — mitigation: rollback + early-fail. Duration ~8 minutes (00:08:12). Impact: elevated streaming tail latency for some customers in prod-us-east-1; ACME impacted (~12% requests >2s) but recovered after rollback. Follow-up: full postmortem and code patch.
David Ortiz: handing off to follow-up rotation. I'm still available for review.
Emma Li: CS offered ACME a 2-day credit; they requested a postmortem and timeline.
Alice Chen: postmortem will be posted at /docs/postmortems/1772009999-fp8-dequant-kv-contention.md in ~2 hours.
Samir Patel: also add a monitoring alert for dequantize wait > 100ms per shard and a canary rollout metric that blocks >1% streaming error/regression.
David Ortiz: thanks all. Closing this incident thread; will comment again after postmortem is published.
